text: Thank you for coming to the teahouse. I liked how easy it was to talk with you.

then.text: I saved the window seat in my memory. It felt like our first little tradition.

name: mai/chapter1/postcard
alt: The map's riverside route drawn on a postcard
caption: The last line follows the river.

options.label: Let's take the riverside route sometime.
options.say: I'd like to walk by the river with you.

then.text: I'd like that. The garden path is quiet at sunset.

options.label: Show me how you drew this map.
options.say: Tell me how you made this route.

then.text: I mark places where I felt at ease. I hope this one becomes another.

text: Quick question: where did we meet for tea?

questions.hint: It was the first stop on the map.

answers.reply: Right. I saved the window seat.

questions.q: What was drawn on the postcard?
questions.hint: Look at the photo from the first chapter.

answers.reply: No, it is more romantic than that.

pass.text: You remembered. That makes me feel seen.

then.text: Both answers on the first try. You were listening.

text: I like thoughtful questions, and I am interested in window gardens. Rushed plans make me nervous.

then.text: I feel comfortable making another plan with you.

otherwise.text: We can keep getting to know each other at our own pace.

then.text: The Riverside Garden is on our next route. The After hours scene in Places opens the path.

name: mai/chapter1/window
alt: A small plant on a bright windowsill
caption: A little green thing to remember the day by.
